name: Flat-fee caption and transcript backlog for small-government meeting video
buyer: Clerks or IT contacts at small municipalities, special districts and school boards that post council or board meeting video
pain: Public video needs accurate synchronized captions under the DOJ Title II rule. Small entities now have until April 2028, and manual minute-writing still takes 8-24 staff hours per meeting.
wedge: Caption and transcribe a district's whole prerecorded YouTube meeting archive for a one-time fee instead of a monthly plan, with a short human review pass.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: Speech-to-text drafts the captions and transcript, and the clerk only reviews them, which the notes estimate at 1-2 hours. This is an estimate and has not been tested.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If buyers already get automated drafts from BoardBreeze or ClerkMinutes with a similar review time, or procurement rules block a one-time purchase from an unregistered vendor, there is no edge.

substitutesNoted.name: City Transcripts
substitutesNoted.price_point: free two-week trial; paid price not found

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: The price is the midpoint of an estimated $300-600 one-time fee per entity. The margin is the midpoint of the 60-75% estimate. Compare BoardBreeze Pro at about $1,188/year. Accuracy QA time is unverified.

majorUncertainty: Whether small government buyers can be reached cold and will pay for a one-time backlog while the deadline is extended, with no references.
unknowns: Actual procurement and vendor-registration thresholds for small entities
Caption accuracy achievable without human editing
No named complaint threads were found
Whether a one-time fee is wanted over a subscription
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on the DOJ Title II timeline. The caption accuracy standard applies, and local procurement or vendor registration may apply. Source video usually sits on YouTube.
